newsitem.title: USA: Dismissed juror says he thinks Simpson is guilty.
newsitem.headline: Dismissed juror says he thinks Simpson is guilty.

text.p: An alternate juror who was dismissed this week from the O.J. Simpson civil trial said on Thursday he believed Simpson was responsible for the deaths of Nicole Brown Simpson and her friend, Ronald Goldman.
"I didn't hear the whole case but ... from what I have heard up to now, I would have to go with guilty," Gilbert Bustillos said on NBC's "Today Show."

Bustillos, who had served as an alternate to the 12-person jury, was dismissed by Judge Hiroshi Fujisaki on Tuesday. He had violated Fujisaki's rules by mentioning the fact that he was on the Simpson case in a Christmas card to a friend.
Simpson was acquitted in October 1995 in criminal court of murdering his ex-wife and Goldman. He is fighting a wrongful death civil suit brought by the families of the victims.
Bustillos said he found Simpson's recent testimony, in which the former football star denied ever hitting Nicole Simpson, unconvincing.
"I didn't believe him, everything he said. He denied everything. He denied knowing about the cuts (on his hand), he denied ever striking or slapping his wife," Bustillos said.

"Anything that they brought up negative, he denied or didn't know. That just didn't go with me," he said, adding," When they were were showing Nicole's pictures, calls to the police, other people's testimony about what they had seen, it didn't fit."
Bustillos said he would have had an easier time believing Simpson if he had admitted losing his temper at least once.
"He denied everything. It just didn't fit. I could have probably swallowed it a little better if he said 'I lost control one day and I backhanded her or something.'
"But just the fact that everything was denied or he didn't know, meant to me he was just trying to bail (out) on everything," Bustillos said.
Simpson was questioned by the plaintiffs' lawyers last month, but defence attorneys chose to cross-examine him at a later date. He could take the stand as early as Friday.
Bustillos' dismissal has left just four of the original eight alternates on the jury panel.
